title: Get Involved
subtitle: Help Build the Community These Frameworks Envision
heroIntro: These frameworks exist as carefully-designed blueprints awaiting the people to bring them to life. Whether you're a community organizer, technologist, funder, translator, or advocate—there's a role for you in transforming vision into reality.

currentState.title: Where This Actually Stands
currentState.paragraph1: Global Governance Frameworks is not a registered organization. There is no staff, no board, no bank account, and no budget. It is one person's project—Björn Kenneth Holmström, working with AI systems for drafting, critique, and adversarial testing—published openly for anyone who finds it useful.
currentState.paragraph2: The frameworks themselves are substantial and carefully researched. What doesn't exist yet is a community around them. If something here resonates with you, you would be early—which means your contribution shapes what this becomes rather than fitting into something already decided.

whyContribute.title: Why Contribute?
whyContribute.paragraph1: The governance challenges facing humanity require collaborative innovation. Current international systems weren't designed for the interconnected crises we face—climate breakdown, pandemic risks, economic inequality, technological disruption.
whyContribute.paragraph2: These frameworks offer practical blueprints for governance that can work at multiple scales while respecting local autonomy. Your skills, perspective, and experience can help create the tools and networks needed for more cooperative, effective governance systems.
whyContribute.paragraph3: There is also a plainer reason. A single person can write frameworks, but a single person cannot test them, translate them, argue with them properly, or carry them anywhere. Whatever this becomes depends on who shows up.

pathways.title: Ways to Contribute
pathways.intro: Choose the contribution path that fits your skills, interests, and available time. Every contribution matters, whether it's translating a single page, testing a framework in your community, or dedicating significant time to implementation.

translationDescription: Help make these frameworks accessible worldwide by translating content into your language. Even partial translations increase accessibility for non-English speaking communities.

translationDetails.why: These frameworks address global challenges and need to be readable in more than one language. Translation isn't just technical work—it's adaptation that makes ideas usable in different cultural contexts.
translationDetails.how: Choose frameworks or pages that interest you, translate at your own pace, and submit contributions through GitHub or email. No formal commitment required—every translated section helps.
translationDetails.skills: Fluency in English and another language, care for accuracy and cultural appropriateness. Understanding of governance concepts helps but isn't required.

websiteDescription: Contribute to the technical infrastructure, build new features, and improve the platform that hosts this work. From bug fixes to major features—all contributions welcome.

websiteDetails.why: The website is the primary interface for these frameworks. Better tools mean better accessibility, easier implementation, and clearer communication of complex ideas.
websiteDetails.how: The codebase is open-source on GitHub. Fork the repository, make improvements, submit pull requests. The site is SvelteKit with a custom schema-driven content system and mdsvex for long-form documents.
websiteDetails.skills: Web development (SvelteKit, JavaScript, CSS), design sensibility, accessibility awareness, interest in governance and systems thinking.

outreachDescription: Share the work, build networks, and connect these frameworks with communities that might benefit from them. Help grow this from a set of documents into a conversation.

outreachDetails.why: Even good frameworks remain theoretical without people who know about them and communities willing to try them. Outreach is what turns blueprints into something anyone can act on.
outreachDetails.how: Share frameworks where they're relevant, write about them, connect with governance innovators, organize local discussion groups, adapt concepts for specific audiences.
outreachDetails.skills: Communication, networking, understanding of social movements, cultural awareness, and a tolerance for explaining early-stage work honestly.

frameworksDescription: Create new governance frameworks, refine existing ones, test implementations, and document what you learn. Help expand the ecosystem with your domain expertise.

frameworksDetails.why: The frameworks have been stress-tested against hostile scenarios, but almost never against reality or against people who disagree from experience. Outside expertise is the missing input.
frameworksDetails.how: Propose new frameworks in your area of expertise, challenge or refine existing ones, document case studies, contribute technical specifications, or simply write up where you think something is wrong.
frameworksDetails.skills: Domain expertise, systems thinking, governance experience, writing ability, willingness to iterate and to disagree in public.

fundingDescription: There is currently no way to donate to this project. That's a deliberate consequence of having no legal entity, and this explains what's being done about it.

fundingDetails.why: Writing, maintaining, and translating this much material takes time that has to come from somewhere. But money can't be accepted responsibly without somewhere accountable for it to land.
fundingDetails.how: Nothing is open yet. An application to a fiscal host is pending, which would allow contributions to be received and accounted for without first forming an association.
fundingDetails.whatNeeded: Development time, translation, and hosting costs — in that order. Larger institutional support would need either a fiscal host or a registered entity first.

implementationDescription: Apply these frameworks in real contexts—your community, organization, or region. Test what works, document what doesn't, share what you find.

implementationDetails.why: Frameworks remain theoretical until tested somewhere real. Implementation reveals what works, what needs rethinking, and what was never going to survive contact with people.
implementationDetails.how: Choose frameworks relevant to challenges you already face, adapt them to your context, implement with community participation, and document the experience—including the failures.
implementationDetails.skills: Community organizing, governance experience, systems thinking, cultural sensitivity, willingness to experiment and report back honestly.

researchDescription: Contribute academic rigor, policy analysis, feasibility studies, and evidence-based refinement. Help strengthen frameworks with research and evaluation.

researchDetails.why: Research can validate approaches, identify problems, and improve design—especially where the frameworks currently rest on reasoning rather than evidence.
researchDetails.how: Provide policy analysis, develop economic models, evaluate proposals against existing literature, contribute legal scholarship, or review frameworks for cultural appropriateness.
researchDetails.skills: Research methodology, domain expertise, academic writing, ethical research practices, commitment to participatory approaches.

globalImpact.title: Global Impact Through Local Action
globalImpact.paragraph1: These frameworks are designed to enable coordination from local to planetary scales. A contribution of any size—one translated page, one framework tested in one community, one well-argued objection—moves the work further than it can go on its own.
globalImpact.paragraph2: The scope is deliberately large. The current reality is deliberately stated. Both are true at once, and holding them together is part of the work.

getStarted.title: Ready to Get Started?
getStarted.paragraph1: Choose whatever fits your skills, time, and interests. There are no applications, approvals, or commitments. Everything here is openly licensed—use it, change it, share it, argue with it.
getStarted.paragraph2: The Discord server is the easiest place to start. It's small and new, which means you can ask a question and get an answer from the person who wrote the thing you're asking about.

communityNote.title: Building Together
communityNote.paragraph1: This isn't a hierarchy where someone at the top decides who may contribute and how. It's an open project where anyone who sees value in the work can participate on their own terms.
communityNote.paragraph2: If a community grows here, coordination tools, communication channels, and governance structures can be built collaboratively—by the people who need them rather than in advance of them.
communityNote.paragraph3: The "we" used throughout these frameworks doesn't describe an existing organization. It names the community the work is inviting. Right now that community is very small. You're part of it the moment you choose to engage.

fundingPage.title: Funding & Resources
fundingPage.subtitle: There's Nowhere to Send Money Yet
fundingPage.heroIntro: The honest version first: you cannot currently donate to Global Governance Frameworks. There is no legal entity, no bank account, and no open funding channel. This page explains why that is, what's being done about it, and what support would actually be useful once a channel exists.

transparency.title: Current Status: No Entity, No Channel
transparency.text: GGF is an open-source project maintained by one person. It is not incorporated, holds no funds, and cannot accept grants, issue receipts, or offer tax deductibility. An application to a fiscal host is pending — a fiscal host would make it possible to receive and account for contributions without first registering an association. Until that comes through, every button on this page that looks like it should take money is switched off. Earlier versions of this site described a bootstrap phase already underway. That was aspirational rather than accurate, and this page corrects it.

needs.title: What Support Would Actually Buy
needs.intro: Listed in the order it would be used, so you can judge whether it's worth funding rather than take a claim on trust.
needs.item1Desc: Hours spent on frameworks, code, translation, and documentation. This is one person's time, and it is the binding constraint on everything else.
needs.item2Desc: Hosting, domains, and collaboration tools. Small, ongoing, and currently paid out of pocket.
needs.item3Desc: Paying translators. The frameworks are only useful to people who can read them, and there is far more English content here than Swedish or Japanese.

conditional.title: Why Not Just Incorporate?
conditional.text: Registering a Swedish non-profit association would solve the bank account problem. It isn't being done, because incorporating needs people rather than paperwork — a board that will hold meetings, keep accounts, and file annual reports. With one person behind it, an entity produces obligations without adding capacity. A fiscal host is the lighter path, which is why it's being tried first. Forming an association becomes worth doing if contributors appear who want to build it.

options.title: Ways to Support
options.githubDesc: Recurring support for the person doing the work, which would go toward dedicated development time rather than overhead. This channel is not open yet.
options.pledgeDesc: If you represent an organization or foundation and want to support this at a scale that would need a legal counterparty, get in touch. Nothing can be accepted today, but knowing the interest exists changes whether formalizing is worth doing at all.

foundingPage.title: If This Becomes an Organization
foundingPage.subtitle: Formalization Is Possible, Not Planned
foundingPage.heroIntro: Global Governance Frameworks isn't a registered organization, and it won't become one on a schedule. Whether it formalizes depends entirely on whether people appear who want to build that structure. This page sets out what that would take.

languageFallback.title: Content in your language coming soon
languageFallback.text: This section is currently displayed in English until translation is complete.

foundingPage.errorText: This page's content could not be loaded. Get in touch directly and the same information can be sent to you.
foundingPage.ctaDescription: No commitment is being asked for at this stage, and no decision has been made that an organization is the right answer. If you have relevant experience — or good reasons to think this is a bad idea — both are worth hearing.
foundingPage.contactDescription: Get in touch to discuss what a founding group would need to look like, or to offer professional advice without joining anything.
foundingPage.missionDescription: Before deciding whether any of this is worth structuring, read what has actually been written. The frameworks are the substance; the organization would only be scaffolding.
